trips.name: Playa Guiones (Nosara) — dry season
trips.note: Arguably the most consistent learner beach break in the Americas (~330 surfable days/yr), warm water, huge surf-school culture. Crowded because everyone knows it. Overhead outside peaks for advanced; Ollie's Point/Witch's Rock boat day-trips.

trips.name: Playa Guiones (Nosara) — green season
trips.note: Peak S-swell, thinner crowds, afternoon rain. Bigger surf trims the beginner score slightly; mornings still user-friendly.

trips.name: Santa Teresa / Mal País
trips.note: Consistent beach breaks for all levels, great food/lodging scene, but discovered — lineups busy and the drive in is long.

trips.name: Tamarindo + Playa Grande
trips.note: Easiest CR logistics, very learner-friendly, boat trips to Witch's Rock. Heavily touristed — the crowd score pays for the convenience.
trips.booking: Easy; book flights early for school weeks

trips.name: Pavones
trips.note: One of the world's longest lefts when a proper S-swell lands — but it needs that swell. Boom-or-bust; remote; limited family lodging.

trips.name: Playa Venao
trips.note: Horseshoe bay that grooms S-swell into all-level peaks; genuinely uncrowded midweek. Sleepy but growing scene.

trips.name: Santa Catalina
trips.note: Powerful world-class right point, empty by CR standards. Estero beach break for learners, but the town is basic and the drive long.

trips.name: Bocas del Toro
trips.note: Caribbean N-swell window — reef and beach options by boat, island-hopping fun. Swell-dependent: flat spells happen.

trips.name: El Zonte + El Tunco (La Libertad)
trips.note: Right-point machine (El Zonte, Sunzal for learners, Punta Roca for experts) 45 min from the airport. Security transformed since 2022; surf-city investment everywhere.

trips.name: Las Flores + Punta Mango (boat resort)
trips.note: Resort-and-panga model: guides run you to Punta Mango when it's on, mellow inside at Las Flores for improvers, pool terrace above the point. The CR experience of 20 years ago.

trips.name: Playa Colorado / Hacienda Iguana
trips.note: Lake-effect offshores ~300 days/yr meet relentless SW swell: barreling beach break at your feet, gated community keeps lineups half-private. Panga trips to Lance's Left/Manzanillo. Political situation is calm in surf zones but score docked.

trips.name: Popoyo
trips.note: Same offshore machine, more variety: Popoyo main peak, Outer Reef for chargers, Beginner's Bay inside. Lodges with pools facing the reef.

trips.name: Playa Maderas (San Juan del Sur)
trips.note: Friendly peaks and a proper learner scene; shuttle-truck culture from SJDS. Busier than the private-community options.

trips.name: El Paredón
trips.note: Uncrowded black-sand beach break village — simple, cheap, consistent. Punchy shorebreak days need supervision for kids.

trips.name: Punta Mita + Sayulita
trips.note: Panga-driven longboard points (La Lancha, Anclote) with genuinely gentle waves; five-star family resorts. Sayulita itself is a zoo — stay Mita side.

trips.name: La Saladita + Troncones
trips.note: Saladita: an endless waist-high left made for learning and longboarding. Troncones/The Ranch up the road for punchy waves. Beach-house rentals with pools.

trips.name: Salina Cruz guided camps (Oaxaca)
trips.note: The 4x4-guide model at its best: sand-bottom right points (Punta Conejo etc.) picked by wind/tide each morning, lineups effectively gated by access. World-class waves; thin beginner options.

trips.name: Puerto Escondido (La Punta base)
trips.note: Zicatela is the Mexican Pipeline — spectate, don't bring the kids out. La Punta and Carrizalillo cove are the family end. Town is buzzing and busy.

trips.name: Los Cerritos / Todos Santos (Baja)
trips.note: Winter NW swell, learner-friendly Cerritos, artsy Todos Santos base. Water is cool (springsuit) and the surf is fun rather than world-class.

trips.name: Scorpion Bay (San Juanico)
trips.note: On a real S-swell: multiple points connecting into minute-long rights, nearly empty. But it needs the swell and getting there is an expedition. Score is honest about the gamble.

trips.name: Costa Azul (San José del Cabo)
trips.note: Resort-corridor convenience with a real summer wave (The Rock, Old Man's for learners). Easy, warm, but lineups concentrate.

trips.name: Rincón
trips.note: The easiest real surf trip from New England: no passport, US healthcare, winter N-swells lighting up a dozen breaks from mellow to Tres Palmas. Swell-dependent weeks and busy peaks are the tax.

trips.name: Playa Encuentro (Cabarete)
trips.note: Dawn-patrol reef peaks that suit surf schools remarkably well; kite/windsurf afternoons for the rest of the family. Short cheap flights.

trips.name: Barbados (Freights + Soup Bowl)
trips.note: Trade-swell island that almost always has something: Freights' gentle left for learners, world-class Soup Bowl for the experts, safe and family-polished everywhere.

trips.name: Chicama + Pacasmayo
trips.note: The longest left on earth: catches any SW swell, and a 2-minute mechanical wall disperses whatever crowd exists. Hotel pools literally overlook the point. Cold-ish water (3/2), grey skies, basic towns.

trips.name: Lobitos + Máncora (north Peru)
trips.note: Desert left points, warmer than Chicama, Máncora has the family beach scene. Oil-town grit around Lobitos.

trips.name: Ayampe + Montañita
trips.note: Warm N-swell season, mellow Ayampe beach break with a quiet yoga-town vibe (skip Montañita's party for the family). Cheap and uncrowded.

trips.name: San Cristóbal (Galápagos)
trips.note: Sea lions in the lineup, N-swell reef points with almost nobody out, plus the wildlife trip of a lifetime for kids. Logistics and cost are the gate.

trips.name: Florianópolis
trips.note: 42 beaches on one island — always a working bank somewhere. Autumn/winter is consistent and less crowded; water cools to springsuit.

trips.name: Itacaré (Bahia)
trips.note: Warm jungle-backed coves with reliable small-to-mid surf — a lovely learn-and-longboard family spot rather than a quality strike.

trips.name: Fernando de Noronha
trips.note: Brazil's Hawaii: crystal N-swell peaks, capped visitor numbers keep it empty, spectacular for kids (dolphins, snorkeling). Expensive and far.

trips.name: Pichilemu / Punta de Lobos
trips.note: Relentless left points, but 4/3-and-booties cold even in summer. A surf trip for a hardy family, not a tropical one.

trips.name: Ericeira
trips.note: World Surfing Reserve: reef points for the experienced, Foz do Lizandro sand for learners, lovely town, red-eye friendly. Everyone in Europe knows it — crowd score suffers.

trips.name: Peniche + Baleal
trips.note: 360° peninsula — some bank is always offshore, from Baleal's learner lagoons to Supertubos. Surf-school capital of Europe, with the lineups that implies.

trips.name: Sagres / Algarve
trips.note: Two coasts at right angles: pick your size and wind every day. Warmer and mellower than Peniche; great family towns.

trips.name: Hossegor + Capbreton
trips.note: The best beach-break barrels on earth in September, croissants for the kids, Capbreton's protected corner for learners. Shifty banks punish beginners on bigger days.

trips.name: Zarautz + San Sebastián
trips.note: Gentle Basque beach breaks, world-best food, culture days built in. A family holiday with very good surf rather than a surf trip.

trips.name: Fuerteventura
trips.note: The 'European Hawaii': winter N-swells, volcanic reefs on the North Track, big sandy Corralejo bay for learners, warm in January.

trips.name: Famara (Lanzarote)
trips.note: Famara's 5km learner beach under the cliffs plus serious reefs (El Quemao) for experts. Reliable winter machine with European ease.

trips.name: São Miguel (Azores)
trips.note: The shortest real flight to empty Atlantic surf from Boston. Black-sand beach breaks and reefs, whales and hot springs for flat days. Weather-roulette — swell and wind change fast.

trips.name: Taghazout + Tamraght
trips.note: Right-point conveyor (Anchor Point, Killers) with a mature surf-camp/guide industry and learner beaches between points. Winter crowds are real now.

trips.name: Imsouane
trips.note: The Bay: a 600m+ gentle right where a first-timer rides for 30 seconds — maybe the best learner wave anywhere. Village amenities are simple; longboarders flock to it.

trips.name: Bundoran + Sligo
trips.note: Cold-water Eden: empty reefs and long beginner strands (Strandhill, Tullan) — in a 4/3 with booties. Family charm high if the family owns wetsuits.

trips.name: Jeffreys Bay
trips.note: Supertubes is the best right point on the planet, and winter delivers it weekly. Learner beaches exist, water's cold, and it's a very long way with kids for a wave only the experts ride.

trips.name: Muizenberg (Cape Town)
trips.note: Surfers' Corner is a legendary learn-to-surf beach, and Cape Town is a spectacular family city. Busy lineups, cool water, shark protocol managed by spotters.

trips.name: North Malé surf resort (Pasta Point/Sultans)
trips.note: Resort-exclusive lineups (Pasta Point caps surfer numbers by design), warm mechanical walls, dhoni boat shuttles, resort pools and lagoons for the family. The model answer to this brief except distance.

trips.name: Central/South atolls resort (Laamu, Six Senses area)
trips.note: Yin Yang and neighbors with a handful out; overwater villas where you watch the sets from the deck. Peak luxury-per-wave, priced accordingly.

trips.name: Weligama–Ahangama south coast
trips.note: Warm, cheap, endlessly mellow — a dozen learner-to-intermediate reefs and beaches in 20km, great food and family villas. Blew up post-2020; lineups show it.

trips.name: Arugam Bay
trips.note: Long sand-bottom right points (Main Point, Whiskey, Peanut Farm) with tuk-tuk guide culture. The far side of a long journey.

trips.name: Uluwatu + Bingin (Bukit)
trips.note: Dry-season perfection every single day — shared with the entire surfing world. The crowd score is the story; cliff-top pools do overlook the breaks.

trips.name: Nusa Lembongan
trips.note: Bali's swell without Bali's chaos: boat-accessed reefs (Playgrounds for improvers, Lacerations for experts), family resorts with pools facing the lineup.

trips.name: Gerupuk + Ekas bays (South Lombok)
trips.note: Boat-to-the-break as daily routine: sheltered bay peaks where every level gets waves every day of dry season. One of the best places on earth to take a mixed-ability crew.

trips.name: Lakey Peak (Sumbawa)
trips.note: A-frame perfection with a pool-bar audience at Lakey's losmen row. More surf-trip than family-trip; long haul.

trips.name: Mentawai land resort (Kandui/HT's zone)
trips.note: The best wave zone on the planet, boat-guided daily, resorts increasingly family-capable. But it's expert-centric, malaria-belt remote, and the journey is brutal with kids.
trips.booking: Resorts 9–12mo; fixed transfers; some exclude under-12s

trips.name: Telo Islands (Resort Latitude Zero)
trips.note: Purpose-built family surf resort: ~20 breaks for a dozen guests, boat-guided by wave-of-the-tide, pool deck facing the surf, kids' programs. The archetype of 'everyone scores daily' — at expedition distance and price.

trips.name: Simeulue Island (Aceh)
trips.note: The quiet Mentawais: mellower reefs (The Peak, Dylan's), a couple of family-run resorts, single-digit lineups. Less wave ceiling, far more forgiving.

trips.name: Nemberala (Rote)
trips.note: T-Land's long forgiving left wall — an intermediate's dream wave — with sleepy-village emptiness and a few good family lodges.

trips.name: Siargao (Cloud 9 + boat breaks)
trips.note: Typhoon-season swell, boat trips to uncrowded reefs beyond Cloud 9, palm-island charm, very affordable. Swell windows less locked-in than Indo; typhoon risk is real.

trips.name: Namotu / Tavarua island resorts
trips.note: Cloudbreak/Restaurants for the chargers, Swimming Pools for improvers, island-capped guest counts, legendary family weeks with kids' programs. As close as it gets to guaranteed world-class waves with a family wrapper.
trips.booking: Named family weeks only (min age otherwise); 12–18mo

trips.name: Coral Coast (Matanivusi / Sigatoka)
trips.note: Eco surf resorts boating you to soft-top-to-serious reef passes with nobody around; gentler and cheaper than the Namotu circus while still Fiji-consistent.

trips.name: Salani / Aganoa (Upolu & Savai'i)
trips.note: Guided-only reef pass culture (resorts hold traditional village access), empty by design. Waves are shallow and punchy — thin true-beginner terrain.

trips.name: Ha'atafu (Tongatapu)
trips.note: A handful of guests, a reef out front, whales breaching behind the lineup Jul–Oct. Shallow reef surfing only; the whale-swim is the family hook.

trips.name: Nusa Island Retreat (Kavieng)
trips.note: The Surf Management Plan caps total surfers per break by law — the only formally rationed lineups on earth. Monsoon-season reefs by boat. Getting there is the hardest itinerary on this list.

trips.name: Pohnpei (P-Pass)
trips.note: Palikir Pass is a dream right for good surfers, boat-only, near-empty. Effectively no beginner terrain — a strike mission wearing a family-trip costume.

trips.name: Waikiki (Oahu) — winter
trips.note: Rescored as Waikiki-only after the audit caught the base-pairing error: the winter row had been charging North Shore quality a mixed family can't ride. Winter south shore is smaller but rideable most days; the North Shore is a spectacular spectator day, not a program. See the summer row for this trip's better family window.

trips.name: Hanalei Bay (Kauai)
trips.note: One perfect crescent: kiddie rollers inside, long point walls outside, US ease, breathtaking setting. Winter surf demands respect on big days.

trips.name: Papara + Moorea (Tahiti)
trips.note: Black-sand river-mouth waves at Papara for improvers, reef passes and the Teahupoo spectacle for experts, overwater-bungalow family glamour on Moorea. Localism is polite but real.

trips.name: Raglan
trips.note: Manu Bay's endless left plus a proper learner beach (Ngarunui), in a green artsy town. Springsuit water in summer; NZ safety and charm.

trips.name: Noosa
trips.note: Perfect sandy points wrapping through a national park — when cyclone swell arrives, and with 200 longboarders. A glorious family beach town whose surf score is hostage to swell roulette and crowds.

trips.name: Nihi Sumba (Occy's Left)
trips.booking: Books 6–12mo; wave capped at ~10 surfers/day; from ~$1.5k/night
trips.note: The brief's platonic ideal, priced accordingly: a formal daily cap on a world-class left, resort-exclusive access, full surf program, and an infinity pool directly over the wave. Beginner terrain is coaching-dependent — sits just under the family gate.

trips.name: Rancho Santana
trips.note: The turnkey answer on the SW Nicaragua corridor the index already loves: five private-access beaches, on-site Surf Club (quiver, coaches, daily program), pools and ranch — beginner sand at Los Perros, Panga Drops/Colorado in guided range.

trips.name: Mizata Resort (western La Libertad)
trips.note: A near-private cove-and-point 45 min west of the El Tunco crowds, with the pool literally overlooking the break, on-site boards and coaching, and the same 9-consistency S-swell window as the rest of the coast.

trips.name: Miramar / Aserradores (The Boom)
trips.note: Same offshore machine as Popoyo, far emptier: The Boom's world-class A-frame for the chargers, mellower inside banks for improvers, and camps that run boards, boats, and the daily call.

trips.name: Banyak Islands (Treasure Island)
trips.note: The budget Telos: tiny island resorts, boat-served zone, near-empty lineups, and Gunturs — a long forgiving right that's one of Sumatra's best learner-to-intermediate waves — on the doorstep.

trips.name: Cabo Ledo
trips.booking: Surf lodges bookable; Luanda transit; e-visa
trips.note: The audit's biggest coastline find: a near-Chicama-consistency 300m mellow left, effectively empty, with all-inclusive surf lodges — one directly fronting the point. Beginner and expert ride the same wave. Luanda logistics and thin medical are the caps.

trips.name: Dakhla
trips.note: Desert surf resorts steps from near-empty right points, with a 40km flat lagoon as the built-in kids' guarantee no other Africa trip has. Wind is the tax — mornings work.

trips.name: San Onofre + Doheny (San Clemente)
trips.booking: Easy; state-park passes; camps and rentals
trips.note: The canonical US family-longboard trip: Old Man's rollers, Doheny for the kids, Trestles in walking range for the chargers. Everything easy, everyone there — the Waikiki crowd logic applies in full.

trips.name: Papatura Island Retreat
trips.note: Family-run island surf resort with daily boats to uncrowded fun reefs — the only family-gate-passing trip in the entire Nov–Apr remote-Pacific window, which the calendar otherwise cedes to experts-first Kavieng and Pohnpei.

trips.name: Ngor + Yoff (Dakar)
trips.note: Two-coast peninsula — swell always hitting one side — with Ngor Right of Endless Summer fame, established island camps doing boards and guiding, and Yoff sand for learners.

trips.name: Waikiki (Oahu) — summer
trips.note: The better family window the winter row obscured: south-shore swell season, Queens and Canoes at their most consistent, and a flat, snorkel-safe North Shore. Beach-boy turnkey at its purest; the crowd is the whole tax.

trips.name: Tamarindo + Playa Grande — green season
trips.note: The Nosara-split logic applied to its neighbor: peak S-swell, thinner crowds, cheaper rooms, school-summer timing. Mornings stay learner-friendly; afternoon rain.

trips.name: Santa Teresa — green season
trips.note: Same beach breaks, more swell, meaningfully fewer people than the listed Dec–Apr window.

trips.name: Namotu / Tavarua — off-season
trips.booking: Easier availability than peak; cyclone-season risk
trips.note: The #1 trip's quiet half: cyclone-season swell roulette trims consistency, but the boats, kids' programs, and Swimming Pools all still run, availability opens up, and prices drop a band. Fills the thin Nov–Mar calendar.

trips.name: El Zonte + Sunzal — small season
trips.note: The beginner-optimal El Salvador window: waist-to-head points, offshore mornings, Sunzal at its most learnable, and the crowds gone with the big swells.

trips.name: Peniche + Baleal — early summer
trips.note: Pre-crowd Baleal: small consistent windswell on the learner lagoons, long days, half the September lineup. Lower ceiling than the autumn row — a gentler version of the same trip.

trips.name: Waco Surf (wave pool) — BENCHMARK
trips.booking: Book sessions online; private hire available
trips.note: Not a surf trip — a calibration row. Perfect scheduled waves, lifeguards, on-site casitas and a lazy river. It outscores every ocean trip, which is the point: it shows what the weights literally optimize for, and why 'it's actually the sea' is the one dimension the model doesn't price. Flagged benchmark; excluded from tiers and the calendar.
